instruction: Choose a suitable finite-element simulation tool available in the current Windows fused environment. The task must be completed through an interactive graphical workflow. Use the the selected finite-element tool the graphical analysis environment GUI to complete a Steady-State Thermal analysis. Physical problem: One-dimensional steady-state heat conduction through a rectangular steel block. Coordinate system and geometry: - Use the global Cartesian coordinate system. - The heat conduction direction is the global X direction. - The block length is along the X direction. - The block occupies: - 0 ≤ X ≤ 100 mm - 0 ≤ Y ≤ 10 mm - 0 ≤ Z ≤ 10 mm - The left end face is the face at X = 0 mm. - The right end face is the face at X = 100 mm. Model parameters: - Block size: 100 mm × 10 mm × 10 mm - Material: Structural Steel - Use steady thermal material properties for steel: - Thermal conductivity k = 50 W/(m·K) - Use a consistent unit system in the graphical analysis environment. - Use a mesh that includes nodes or elements on the mid-length section at X = 50 mm. Boundary conditions: - Left end face at X = 0 mm: - Prescribed temperature = 100 °C - Right end face at X = 100 mm: - Prescribed temperature = 20 °C - All other external faces are adiabatic. Analysis type: - Steady-State Thermal analysis. Deliverables: save the native model artifact and native solver result artifact on the Desktop.
